utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-84-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Before we ask the Prosecution to call its next witness, I'd like to make a few observations. First of all, the parties should keep in mind that Witness 3, which is the witness next to the one who will appear first, should be done by the end of Wednesday. That's clear to everyone so that we make a joint effort to take care that he is able to leave in time. Before the next witness comes in, we'll go into private session, even for a while in closed session, in view of the still-pending motion for protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then as far as Witness 3's protective measures are concerned, I was informed although I have not yet carefully read that none of the three Defence counsel objects to the protective measures asked for the last -- the Defence for Mr. Brahimaj confirming this. Then there is a recently filed motion for the Prosecution's fourth motion for testimony via videolink which was filed today. In view of the urgency of the matter, the Chamber would very much like the Defence to make submissions by tomorrow, 5.00, not later. I can imagine looking at the request that you would like to make written submissions. Then, I still have a decision to deliver on the protective measures for Witness 17. May I take it that all the booths have received copies? It is not the decision but these are the reasons for the Chamber's decision on the Prosecution's motion for protective measures for Witness 17. On the 27th of August, 2007, the Prosecution applied for retention of the pseudonym granted during the pre-trial phase of this case, and for face and voice distortion for Witness 17. The Defence did not oppose the motion and the Chamber granted it on the 28th of August 2007. As the Chamber has stated on prior occasions, the party seeking protective measures for a witness must demonstrate an objectively grounded risk to the security or welfare of the witness or the witness's family should it become known that the witness has given evidence before the Tribunal. This standard can be satisfied by showing that a threat was made against the witness or the witness's family. According to the motion, Witness 17 has numerous contacts with the Prosecution expressed concerns about his and his family's safety as a result of his scheduled testimony before the Tribunal. As specified in the motion, threats have been directed against the witness and a member of his family. The Chamber considers that the witness's fear is genuine and objectively based and that there is a risk that if the testimony of the witness were to be made public, physical harm might result to the witness or the witness's family. This concludes the Chamber's reasons for its decision on this matter. Then the Chamber would like first to proceed with discussing the protective measures for the witness now to be called. It might be that Mr. Dutertre, before we ask the witness in -- would you like to add anything to what was submitted before?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. First of all, I wish to have your own directions on the point of knowing whether the witness should be called in number 3 this afternoon or not. I will myself be quite brief with the next witness. I don't know for the Defence teams. But it would be useful for the protection of the witness to know whether he has -- whether Witness number 3 has to wait for this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now I remember that indication was given earlier to the Chamber. You said you would need not more than 15 minutes at least on the basis of an agreement on the 92 ter statement. I think we dealt with all of that at the Friday early morning meeting and I think Defence counsel would not need the whole of this afternoon. Mr. Emmerson?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: For my part, I think I indicated a maximum of 45 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Absolutely, we won't be that long.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Certainly won't either, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And therefore, there is a reason for Witness 3 to stay because there is a fair chance that he'll be called this afternoon. One second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. For the next witness to be called, protective measures have been asked. That is, pseudonym, face distortion, voice distortion. The Defence counsel have not made any submissions on this request, as far as I remember. Mr. Emmerson?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very shortly, we respectfully submit that the motion as it stands does not satisfy the standard for the grant of the protective measures sought. Plainly the matter can be explored with the witness if that is deemed necessary or appropriate as has been the case with other professional witnesses, if I can use that term to describe those whose function it is to assimilate, acquire and record evidence and then testify in relation to it. The essential position, as described, is that this is a witness who -- whose family still has property in Kosovo but has apparently has no concrete plans to return there and is concerned and has expressed himself concerned primarily about financial implications. That I recall is an approach that's been advanced to advocate it on behalf of other witnesses who are party to this part of the investigation and so far has not resulted in a grant of protective measures and we would respectfully submit that as matters currently stand, justification is not made out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I join.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I do too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour this witness wished for protective measures and the reason we filed this motion in the annex AA to this motion in paragraph 4, we mention the possibility to come back and live in Kosovo for this witness. And this is definitely one of the points which requires more questions be asked from the witness. I know what are the criteria given by the Chamber on this matter, of course. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I then suggest that we further hear from the witness. To that end, I think the curtains should be down, because -- has any test been made in relation to the voice distortion so that if the Chamber would decide that it's prepared for or is there not, Mr. Dutertre? Voice distortion usually takes some time to prepare for. We earlier have had situation in which the party seeking protective measures, especially if it's voice distortion, already makes a test so that we don't lose time later. Of course, I cannot anticipate on what the decision will be but I just established at this moment that if we would order a voice distortion that the technical preparation has not yet been performed. Could the curtains be taken down and could we move into it would be closed session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness 64, the Chamber has decided to grant the protective measures as requested. That means that your face cannot be seen by the outside world, your voice cannot be heard by the outside world. We'll call you Witness 64 and not use your own name. These protective measures, that is pseudonym, voice and face distortion, does not mean that your testimony cannot be heard. The contents of your testimony can be heard by those who are following the proceedings. If there is any question where you feel the need to ask for private session, that you are concerned about perhaps the implications, security implications, on the basis of your answer, you can indicate so and the Chamber will then decide whether or not for that specific question go into private session, which, if so decided, would mean that the outside world cannot hear the content of your testimony either. You'll now first be examined by Mr. Dutertre who is counsel for the Prosecution. The Mr. Dutertre, the Chamber has not yet received a new 92 ter statement or did we?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it should be on e-court this morning, with the redactions, both for the English and Serbian version. Perhaps the Chamber hasn't received it yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because it's uploaded on e-court that doesn't automatically mean that the Chamber can inspect whatever is uploaded by any of the parties, so therefore, under those circumstances perhaps the first thing to do is perhaps either to provide us with a hard copy or to ask admission right away so that we can consult it on our screens. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. There is a hard copy for the witness but I have no other for the moment. I could, of course, give mine, my own.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One of them being that the version you uploaded to have that assigned a number as quickly as possible so that we can follow it on our screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I request the version of the (redacted) in order to get a P number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, do you know what document we are talking about? If you have a 92 -- if you have a 65 ter number or any other document identification, then the registrar could --

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's number 65 ter 1959. 1959, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P907, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P907. Thank you, please proceed, Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I would now like to show to Witness 64 document concerning his identity and his name. Therefore, pseudonym sheet 1964.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Number --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be Prosecution Exhibit P912.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P912 not to be shown on the screen. Also the 65 ter statement not to be shown on the screen. Please proceed, Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would it be possible to give a hard copy to the witness so that he may authentify it?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Witness 64, you have a document which states your identity. Is all this exact, true and correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Usher. You can take the document back. You could give the 92 ter document to the witness in this folder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Usually, Mr. Dutertre, it is shown on our e-court screen so that the Chamber also has a possibility to understand the -- yes -- answer of the witness. A hard copy, of course, would do now as well but it's more easy to put it on the screen so that we don't have to run up and down the -- but --

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. It's possible to show, 1964, which can be exhibited and it will remain confidential.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: (redacted) Witness 64, do you confirm that what you can see on the screen is correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I confirm that it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness 64, you have a folder, a blue folder, with a certain number of documents. It is your edition in English and in Serbian and annexes which go with these documents. Is this the interview you gave to the Prosecution on 23, 24 October 2007?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. This is all correct and this is the document indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, I don't know whether or not there was a mistranslation somewhere but I believe that at least on line 16 it says October and I believe it should be August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know where it comes from but I take it that August was meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is August, indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Please once more the complete dates? Is there more than one day?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 23, 24 and 27 August 2007.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Witness 64, [In English] Reflects your declaration and what you would say if you were to be asked questions in court today about the same issues?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I would definitely say the same things.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I confirm my request to have this document filed in its --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Version of the 92 ter statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tendered.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think Your Honour is an aware that certain objections were made and the document has been edited in accordance with Your Honour's rulings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The present version which I still haven't seen is not objected to. Mr. Guy-Smith, the same?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That is correct. I would once again reassert the concerns we had about paragraphs 112 through 115.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Harvey, the same position, as far as I understand. Then, please proceed, Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Redactions were made following the discussions we had, and I remember that for paragraph 112 and 115 no decision was made to redact.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Witness 64, [In English] Now have your written statement before them as your evidence and Defence counsel may wish to ask you some questions but before that, I have very few questions. Page -- page 13, paragraph [Interpretation] Paragraphs 77 in the English version and paragraph 15 in the Serbian version, you indicate, and this can be shown on the screen, but this will be exhibited under seal, you say: [In English] "On 12 September 1998, I video recorded a small plastic evidence bag labelled R19 -- 19, containing body parts which I believe belonged to Tush Frrokaj. Tush Frrokaj, identified at a later stage together with his wife. I believe this was the case based on my recollection and this is further confirmed by the video recording; the Trial Chamber also has access to the forensic experts' reports so they can check the allegations contained in my statement." [Interpretation] Therefore, page 1577 -- paragraph 77 in your interview, now I would like to have the video.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't catch that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which is P452 from minute 139, 1 hour 39 minutes and 49 seconds, to 1.55 seconds. Could this video be played, please? 1.45.05.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe there is a mistake on the transcript. It was until 1.45 -- 1.40.05, says the interpreter. Could we go backwards a little bit? Could we have the right image on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Witness 64, this bag bearing number 19 is the one you referred to in paragraph 77 of your interview?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me, I would note for the record that for the first time the image as it is presented at 1.40.047 has no date or time on it. So whether or not this is in fact an actual continuous shot or not may be of some question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre? Yes perhaps we could ask the witness and from what I remember from the statement is that sometimes date and time were left out and then reintroduced, which not necessarily affects the sequence of the indication given by the media player by which it is played but perhaps the parties could verify among themselves whether there is any real problem here or whether it's just --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There may well be a real problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then if there is, the Chamber would like to have a clear explanation what the real problem is. But for the time being, let's proceed until the real problem has been properly identified so that the Chamber can deal with it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Chairman.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Witness 64, when was it that you shot the image we can see right now on the screen? What date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This footage was made immediately after the body number 18 was lifted up. That was a woman who was later identified as Illira Frrokaj and that's the footage that precedes this footage that we just saw, where you can see this woman being put into a plastic body bag. In my statement, if you will allow me, indicated quite clearly why there is no date indication in some of the recordings. At that time, I used a VHS camera, it was a Panasonic camera, that did not switch on the date function automatically. It had to do -- had to be done manually. This is when those mistakes occurred resulting in the date indication not appearing on all the footage. It happened until I actually remembered to switch on this function.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, coming back to my previous question, this bag bearing number -- the number 19, is it the one you referred to in paragraph 77 of your statement, written statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have to tell you that it was taken on the 12th of September 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: The bag referred to in paragraph 77 of your statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Precisely. Well, you can't really call it a body bag. It's an evidence bag. And it was labelled 19 because it contained body parts. In practice, it is usually the case that when a body part, an unidentified body part, is found, it is marked DT. But here we have the number that indicates the body, as far as I remember, in fact I'm sure that it was Tush Frrokaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Moving now to another point, and I will -- this is my question before the last one and there will be two questions and I would like document D32 to be displayed now. It's a map so it takes a bit before it can be displayed on the screen. Can we please see, magnify the lower part? My question is the following for the Witness 64. Can you confirm that on the road going from Djakovica to Decani there is a village called Skivjane?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you. You have in the blue folder which I am going to ask you to look at it, you have your statement with the appendices and I would like you to look at appendix 2. These are weather documents in Serbian language. They concerned a period going from March to September 1978 [as interpreted] In the area of Pec and Skivjane. And I would like you more particularly to look at the last page for the Serbian document concerning September 1998. And while you're looking for the document in appendix 2, I would like document 65 ter 1961, the last page of this document, be displayed on the e-court. It's the same document. That's the English version of the document. That's for your own information, Witness 64, this is the -- this is annex 2. That's the Serbian version. So you look at the last page of this document. And maybe we could magnify the document on the screen so as to see the last line in the table. Can you see the document, Witness 64?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: My question is the following: The data -- I repeat my question -- the data you can see here for September 1998, are these data consistent with what you remember about the weather that day in the Skivjane area?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'd object to the form of the question with regard to the data being consistent with his memory of weather. He can testify as to what he remembers the weather to be at that time and then the Chamber can draw its own conclusions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Consistency in such an observation is difficult to follow, Mr. Dutertre, if you do not have the facts underlying such an opinion about consistency.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. First of all, I would like to ask to you display the English version because on the screen we can see the Serbian version which does not allow to you follow since the witness has the hard copy document. No, it seems that it's okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Witness 64, it is indicated -- well, the following is indicated: [In English] From 12 to 14, 22 and 29 September, there was rain in 16 days in September, which with a maximum daily amount, 27.6 millimetre on 13th September. The thunder processes were registered only on 8 September. [Interpretation] Witness 64, do you remember -- or does your memory of the weather in September 1998 allows you to confirm that it was raining on September the 13th, 1998?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Put in that form, and standing alone, I don't object to the question and answer which is why I sat down. What I'm concerned about is the witness being invited to confirm data which is plainly not going to be in a position to confirm, recorded in the document. But if the question is simply was it from your recollection raining on the day, then, frankly, it could be done without reference to the document at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Dutertre, I don't think that the witness could give any details as to in the 10th of millimetres how much rain fell on these days but as you may have noticed there is no objection against exploring the weather at that time. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Well, not mentioning the number of millimetres but I just would like to know whether it was raining in that area in September on the 13th of September 1998.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I can confirm that it was a rainy day, because the next day, on the 14th, we had a problem because there was a flood. If you -- a flash flood. So I remember very well that it was on the 13th, not on the 14th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you is there any dispute about heavy rains on the 13th of September? Apart from what the rain may cause but --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour has seen the evidence and we are not in a position at this stage to dispute or agree but Your Honour has seen the evidence and the challenges that have been raised in relation to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: On the same point, Witness 64, are you in a position to remember whether on September the 8th, 1998, there was any thunder-storm or bad weather as mentioned in this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As for the 8th September, I can't really claim whether there were any thunder-storms on that day, based on my recollection, but from this document from the hydrometeorological institute in Belgrade and some things that I've seen since I've been in touch with you, I can confirm that --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: This is precisely why the objection was interposed at the beginning of this particular colloquy with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre, if the witness reading this says that the document says that on the 8th of September, that only on that date thunder processes were registered, then to ask the witness do you have any recollection and he says no, I've got no recollection but as seen from this document, everybody could see that from this document. Then the next item would be to what extent this document is reliable, and not for the witness to read the document, which everyone can do. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am moving on to another point.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: I would like you to look at annex 3 of your statement, and more particularly the document bearing the number U 0142084 at the top of the page. And while you're looking for this document, I would like to show 65 ter 1962, page 11, on the screen. So for you it is document bearing the number U 0142084, at the top of the page on the right. Well, it would be easier if you look at the Post-it which will allow you to find the document more quickly. Below the picture it is mentioned [In English] "Body of the massacred Supec [phoen], captain of police Perovic, Srdjan, 1962, kidnapped by the Albanian terrorists on 6 July 1998, in the village of Pec, Pecanac and filmed on the 16th August 1998 in the village of Gllogjan. " [Interpretation] My question is the following and this will be my last question, can you confirm that there is a mistake concerning this picture above? This is not Captain Perovic but rather the body of Milo Rajkovic the other pictures being labelled properly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I can confirm that. I understand the question, yes. I can confirm that this is indeed not Captain Srdjan Perovic. Photograph number 1, I don't know whether this label was affixed there by mistake. I don't know who made this mistake but at any rate this is not Captain Srdjan Perovic but this is a reserve police officer, Milo Rajkovic. He was on the force at that time. And the very next photograph does indeed refer to Captain Perovic. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness 64. I have no other questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Dutertre. Mr. Emmerson, are you the first one to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am. I think Your Honour is aware there is a standing objection in relation to the last passage of evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness 64, you'll now be examined by Mr. Emmerson who is counsel for Mr. Haradinaj. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I want to start, if I may, by asking you about the passage in your witness statement that Mr. Dutertre took you to in paragraph 77 and for this purpose could the witness please be provided with the green bundle from the forensics bundles? Now, it would help, Witness 64, if at the same time as looking at your own 92 ter statement that you have attested to in these proceedings, you could have the green bundle open at tab 9, which contains a statement made by you on the 29th and 30th of May 2006. And I want to just ask you about some changes between the two documents. Now, first of all, paragraph 77 in your 92 ter statement is the equivalent of paragraph 78 in the statement you will find behind tab 9 in the green bundle. Can you confirm to us, please, that when you made your original witness statement in respect of that passage of video, you said this: "I videorecorded a body bag with a body inside. I don't know if this body -- this is body labelled R18 or R19." Do you see that passage? ?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There is no need for me to look at it. I can remember all this quite clearly and I can give you my answer right away.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The first question is you agree that that was what you recorded at the time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, on the 23rd of June of this year, did you attend a formal meeting in Belgrade when the text of a witness statement was put to you and you were invited to confirm that the witness statement was correct in all respects and to attest to it so that it could be read to the Trial Chamber without you giving evidence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So in the light of that, I'm going to ask you some questions about some changes that appear between the statement you attested to in June, which is this text, and the statement that you have sworn to today. Now in respect to that same passage of videotape today, you now say in your 92 ter statement that you videorecorded a small plastic evidence bag labelled R19 containing body parts which you believe belonged to Tush Frrokaj. When did you remember that this passage in your statement was incomplete?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir, the moment I looked at the original tape that I personally recorded, and I would like you to contact investigator Kelly and to ask him to give you the CD that he showed me, and to have a look at -- on the CD on your laptop and to see whether you can actually identify this number on the bag because this copy is very, very bad. And that was the reason why at that time I said I was not sure about the label on this small bag. So I would like to ask you once again to look at this copy. You will see indeed that this copy is extremely poor. That is why, later on, I changed some other things that I had given -- I changed my statement in relation to the one that I had given to Mr. Kelly because the copies were very bad. And this is why it is very good that we still have the original VHS recordings which are very good and which are at your disposal so that you can look at them too.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. We've seen the videos and we have had plenty of opportunity to look at them, Witness 64. The question I was asking you was a simple question of time because on the 23rd of June of this year you were given a copy of this witness statement made by you with the text recorded by you in May 2006 and at that time, you attested to its completion. In other words you said it was an accurate statement. So something has obviously occurred to you since you made that declaration; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm just telling you where the problem was. The problem lay in the fact -- well, it is an uncontroversable fact that this compact disk was a very poor copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I interrupt you, please? Again, if you just listen to the question, I'm not asking you for the explanation yet. I'm simply asking you to confirm that the changes that you've made to your statement were made since you attested to the earlier draft as being complete on the 23rd of June of this year.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean. I'm really sorry. I would like to answer your question but I simply can't see what you're driving at. I just don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me put it to you again because it affects a number of passages in your statement. On the 23rd of June of this year, in Belgrade, you attended a formal meeting with a representative of this Court, together with an investigator from the Prosecution called Roel Versonnen and an interpreter. Do you remember that meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I do remember that quite clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And during this meeting, you were given the text of your previous witness statement as well as a number of other documents, weren't you, to look at?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I remember that too.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And were you given an opportunity to read them and to correct in them anything that was wrong, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I was definitely given an opportunity to go through my statement. That statement had been taken in English. And until this moment, I never received -- until that moment I never received the translation into Serbian so, yes, I was given it to read through.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you then signed to indicate that the statement was correct and complete; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Do you mean the statement that was taken last year?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Indeed, the statement that was taken last year, with the same text in it that you see in front of you today, was the statement that you signed on the 23rd of June to indicate that you had read it and it was true and correct.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Even back then, sir, I insisted that changes be made. I don't know if this was due to an error of interpretation or not, but some significant matters were left out of my statement and I asked that they be put back in.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You signed a Serbian translation of this statement, Witness 64, on the 23rd of June?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But you didn't correct this passage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Which one?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Paragraph 78.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What does it refer to? Can you enlighten me, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's right in front of you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's the very short passage in which --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Can you please put the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There is a confusion here. What is on the screen is the 92 ter statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- where it refers at paragraph 77 to the testimony the witness has given. I'm seeking to question him, and he has it as does the Trial Chamber, behind tab 9 in the green file.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: On the equivalent paragraph in his earlier witness statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please, Madam Usher, could you help the witness? Green binder, tab 9, in the B/C/S version --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, this is in Albanian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is Albanian, yes, and then perhaps look at the English version. English version page 13, paragraph 78. I'll read it for you. Have you got it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please go ahead and read.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It reads as follows. It's only two lines. "At 12.22, on the 12th of the 9th of 1998, I video recorded a body bag with a body inside. I don't know if this is body labelled R18 or R19." Now, what Mr. Emmerson would like to know is whether it's true that you did not correct this passage of your statement when you reviewed it on the 23rd of June of this year. That's what Mr. Emmerson would like to know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I didn't correct it, then it must have been my fault. I must have been reading it not carefully enough, and overlooked that passage. I'm sure that the problem lay only in the CD, the quality of which was poor. Had I noticed this point, I would have corrected it right away, I'm sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you then, please, just turn behind tab 2 in the green binder?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now talking about the same binder, Witness 64.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And in the English translation, it's page 85 of the 92 ter statement of Dusan Dunjic which is exhibit P618, and it should be paragraph 441.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you'll find that in the original, page 69.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: This is a record made by the head of the forensic team about R19 and it reads as follows: "This number was used to label a number of civilian items of clothing, both men's and women's that were found on both river banks. There was enough clothing as to belong to several persons, though I cannot guess how many." So the record shows, Witness 64, that bag R19 or exhibit label R19 was a collection of clothing. In your latest witness statement, you have indicated that you have a recollection of it containing body parts belonging to someone identified as Tush Frrokaj; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You see, I trust the footage I myself produced in situ. What Dusan Dunjic is saying, that R-19 was used to mark clothing in my view, is certainly not true. R-19 contains body parts, as can be seen in the footage. You can also look at the photo documentation that you certainly have, and then we can discuss this, but I cannot agree that R-19 was the label used to mark clothing. Definitely not. Otherwise it would be clearly seen in the footage. This was on a rock in the very canal, and there was some clothing there too, and R-19 would have been seen somewhere there, if this had been the case. It is not the case because it refers to body parts. I believe that the photo documentation could help solve this problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Witness 64, there was a body that was misidentified, that is wrongly identified, as the body of Tush Frrokaj, turned out on DNA analysis to be somebody quite different but that body was recorded as having been labelled R-26. Just help us. Is it your testimony that in fact the body that was identified as Tush Frrokaj wasn't labelled R-26 but was labelled R-19?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To my knowledge, R-19, and this is what I say in my statement, and I will not depart from my statement by an inch, I don't know if the DNA analysis perhaps show that R-19 wasn't Frrokaj's body. I know that the couple named Frrokaj was identified in situ based on the vehicle that had been thrown down into the canyon and based on the pieces of clothing. The fact that, as you say, the DNA analysis proved that the body was misidentified is something I don't know anything about. I was on the spot and saw relatives, brothers and sisters, arrive at the scene and identify the married couple, Tush and Illira Frrokaj. I saw that with my own eyes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could we move, please, to paragraph 24? I'm sorry, I do apologise. Yes, paragraph 24 of your 92 ter statement and at the same time, for those of us following in English, paragraph 24 of the witness's 2006 statement behind tab 9 in the green file. I just want to ask you a little bit more detail about this, Witness 64, because in the statement that you attested to on the 23rd of June of this year, I'm going to read to you the words that appear there, and then ask you to compare them to what's in your 92 ter statement. In your 2006 statement, at paragraph 24, in the last few lines, you say this: "In the canyon, I saw a red Opel Kadett car on its roof. Close to the car there were two bodies, a male and a female. The female and male were later identified. They were a married Catholic Albanian couple." And then in the following paragraph, in the original, which has become paragraph 26 in your 92 ter statement, you say, "After the bodies were identified, the family was brought to the scene to view the red Opel Kadett car. They identified the car as belonging to the couple. These bodies were partly burnt." I'm going to take you to two further passages, please, before asking you the question I want to put to you. Paragraph 32 of your original witness statement from last year, which seems to have no comparison at all in the 92 ter statement reads as follows: "The two bodies in the canyon where the red Opel Kadett was located were recovered with the assistance of the fire brigade who gave us a ladder to get down to the canyon and a rope to haul the body bags with the body inside up to ground level." Now, what on the face of it appears clear, Witness 64, is that in the statement that you made last year, and which you attested to being complete on the 23rd of June of this year, you were suggesting that there were two bodies found close to the car, that of a male and a female, but in the 92 ter statement that you've attested to today, the reference to the male has been removed. Can you help us as to how that happened between the 23rd of June and today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I will account for all this, sir, right away. In 2006, when I was first giving my statement, a full eight years had passed since the case. This was quite a long period of time. When I was called to give my statement, I had not had -- I had not consulted the material I had previously produced. I was giving short and clear answers to questions put to me. In my subconscious it was quite clear to me that at the time we had recovered the married couple named Frrokaj. I can clearly describe what the female body looked like at the time and I remember clearly that the male was found some two or three metres away from the female body, that parts of the male body were found. This led me to say in 2006 that the two bodies were indeed in the vicinity of the car. However, when I consulted my original material and went through it step by step, I realised that the male body was not clearly visible on the spot and that's why I changed my statement, in order not to find myself in a predicament in which I'm now, that you're putting unpleasant questions to me. However, there is nothing controversial about it. That's my statement, and I stand by it. If anything I said in my statement does not add up or if you think that I am not presenting them accurately, you have these tapes that you are free to look at and what they show is the truth and only the truth. Let me only add this: You were mentioning a ladder, firefighters' ladder. The problem lay merely in Kelly or the person interpreting because the video footage shows that the height was of less than four metres and there was no need for the ladder to be put down. It had to be put down at Lake Radonjic but not here. We could easily access the area. This is another thing that the video footage shows, that these were not my words. This was why I asked for that part of my statement to be corrected too. As you review the video footage, you will see at one point a ladder placed against a cliff in order for us to reach the bottom of the canyon.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Whilst I'm asking the next question, I wonder if the registrar could pull up 65 ter 870, page 16, please. There is one --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that an exhibit number already?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think it isn't yet exhibited.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not yet, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Before we look at this photograph I wonder if I could just direct your attention to one passage in your statement that you don't seem to have corrected in relation to the male body that you thought you'd remembered seeing. If you look at paragraph 33 of your 92 ter statement that Mr. Dutertre gave you in the little blue file, this is the statement that you attested to this afternoon. You say in the second-to-last sentence -- don't worry about the photograph, Witness 64, for the moment. You say in the second-to-last sentence in paragraph 33 of the statement that you attested to this afternoon, in relation to the two bodies by the car, you say, "I remember the family identified, the female's ring and her sandals but the male's body was almost 80 per cent burned." That is in the statement that you've sworn today is the truth. Is that right? Was there a male body almost 80 per cent burned, Witness 64?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct. Evidently, this was a male body that was more than 80 per cent burnt. You have to understand my position, sir, too. When I'm out in the field filming with my camera, I'm concentrating on the work I'm doing in order to record as many details as possible. It is only later when I review the material that I filmed, I notice a number of things that I had not noticed earlier. You can ask any cameraman doing the same job about whether this is the case. It is only after a cameraman reviews the material he filmed back in his office that he will notice a number of details. Why? Simply because the person doing that work has to concentrate, focus, on the work he's doing in order to record as many details as possible. I think it must be quite clear to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness 64, you earlier talked about nasty questions. You take a very defensive approach in answering the questions. Mr. Emmerson just tries to find out about all the details. There is no need to explain that it's not as bad as you seem to hear in the questions of Mr. Emmerson. Let's just look at the material, let's see whether we can clarify any remaining questions that are raised. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Witness 64, there was no male's body that was 80 per cent burned recorded as having been recovered from the canal. So can I put the question to you again? Do you recall seeing two to three metres from the car, as you said in your statement made last year, a male body that was 80 per cent burnt? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I've just given you an explanation about the body of Tush Frrokaj. I know that his lady was found by the car. I know that he was identified on the site, and I know that it was close to her body that his body parts were identified. When I was giving my statement, I said yes, I saw her and him lying by the car. It was almost a mechanical automatic answer. And this was, of course, a full eight years later. However, when I took the material from the MUP, sat down and reviewed it, I realised that the body was not to be seen there, and that was when I corrected myself. I don't know if you understand what I am saying. But this is the way it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can we look now at the photograph that's on the screen, please? And might that be marked for identification?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, that would be number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D159, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You invited us earlier on to compare your testimony about R-19 with the photographic evidence. There it is. The number 19 having been allocated to a collection of clothing. Now, Witness 64, would you like to revise your testimony at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can see quite clearly that number 19 is labelling -- or rather labels the clothing, but then I'm asking you in turn what of the evidence bag and the body parts? You can see that there is a letter label too, I can see it here, and why don't we look at that, what that is all about? You see, to the left of number 19, there is this cone with a letter on it. I'm sure it must mean something.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. We know what the cone means and you'll remember it yourself, Witness 64. It's a letter R that was being used to identify the exhibits by R number. And the testimony you gave us earlier on --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- was that R-19 was a body bag with a body inside it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This question was already asked and the witness already answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is a matter where looking at photographs that there might be good reason to further explore whether, and if so when, and by whom, a mistake was made. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I just want to be clear, looking at that again, is it still your testimony that the body labelled -- I'm sorry, the exhibit labelled R-19 was a bag containing body parts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, of course. I stand by the view that these were body parts, yes. In my statement, I even placed a caveat in -- by saying that the Trial Chamber had at their disposal all of the documentation, and were free to see what this was all about. This is something I stated in my statement, that there were documents that can be consulted and -- and on that basis one can conclude whether what I said was correct or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. If your recollection is clear, Witness 64, it would appear to suggest that the same exhibit label was being used for two different things, a body which has disappeared because it's not on any of the records, and a collection of clothing which is shown in the photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness is being asked to -- this question is purely speculative.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: There was overlapping.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I won't pursue it. I'm in the Trial Chamber's hands as to how far you would wish to pursue this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. One second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would have one additional question for the witness. Could you please look at the screen carefully? You see that there is the cone with number 19. If you look at the top corner of this, what looks from here, triangle, there is some black thing, more or less horizontally which stretches until the legs of the person right to number 19. Could you tell us from your recollection what that is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Obviously, this is a body bag.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson and Mr. Dutertre, I'm looking at both of you. There seems to be something which looks a bit like plastic and is close to where number 19 is. My recollection doesn't serve me well enough to know whether we have any other photographs where this plastic -- whatever, or at least looks like a plastic item, is sufficiently explained but... You see what I mean? I'm talking about the black item with some folds in it which is behind the two feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It may be that we can research the point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Because there seems to be quite a lot of disagreement here on what relates to 19. I wasn't there so I wouldn't know, but I notice that there is at least one object close to 19 which has the appearance of a plastic --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If I'm not mistaken, I thought that the beginning of Mr. Dutertre's examination, where he showed that series of videos, whether there is an undated or timed bag was the bag that he was alluding to as being R-19. For this witness's examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I'm just looking at this photograph now and I'm asking myself this question, and we have heard the witness, who several times insisted on that 19 was related to a body bag and not just to a couple of clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour has seen the passage I've put to him from Dusan Dunjic's report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We simply have no other testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I earlier -- -- well, we have the testimony of this witness and the testimony of Professor Dunjic where there seems to be quite some inconsistency. Which, of course, earlier when you said, Mr. Dutertre, that the question had been asked, the question had been answered, that under the present circumstances, that it might be a good thing to further explore whether, when and by whom any mistakes were made. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you turn, please --

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand that Mr. Guy-Smith has indicated that in the video clip which was shown, there was first an R-19 bag and the witness specified at the beginning of the video it was the R-18 body but the witness indicated this specifically.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If need be, we could always look again at that video to -- because our attention is now especially drawn to this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could we look, please, behind tab 8, Witness 64? This is a witness statement made by a colleague of yours, and I'll pause to see if any objection is taken to the use of the name. I think it's been used before. If we could please look to paragraph 18, I'm afraid we don't have it in B/C/S but only in English and Albanian in the bundle. This is a witness statement made by Goran Jovovic. You worked with him on this operation, did you not, Witness 64? I'm going to read to you an extract from his --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm going to read to you an extract from his witness statement, where he says this: "At the beginning of the natural part of the canal, one car was found in the water. In the trunk of this car, an Opel Kadett, the body of a woman who later turned out to be Illira Frrokaj, was found. I remember that it was the body which was labelled number 18 during the course of the exhumation. The trunk was opened by me," and there is then a name given which is your name. "After succeeding to open it, we found a completely naked woman therein." Witness 64, did you find the naked body of a woman inside the trunk of the car, yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, never. You have my -- you have it that I arrived on the site on the 11th, and you have the recording of the female body being found on that very same day. So I never had any physical contact with the car itself. And as for Jovovic's statement, I don't know where he got that. Believe me, my brief was to video record things. For all the other physical work, moving the car, digging and so on, people from the municipal company were supposed to do that. I had nothing to do with the car. I had -- I never touched the car. And why shouldn't I say now before the Court that I found bodies in the trunk? Had that been the case I would have said that but this is definitely not true at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you be shown, please, the blue file for a moment? And whilst that is coming to you, Witness 64, you mention in your 92 ter statement, at paragraph 8 and paragraph 39, some photographs showing bodies that you say were not there by the time you arrived. I'm not asking you for any comments or explanation. But I'm asking you to confirm, please, if you look behind tab 1, first of all, by the time you arrived on the scene, the two sets of human remains that are shown behind tab 1 in the blue file, this is Exhibit D31, were not in that location.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct. On the 11th of September, those bodies were not there on the site.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you now turn, please, behind tab 4, where you will find two photographs of the same body, that is to say not the two bodies we've looked at before but two different photographs of the same body? And can I ask you, please, to confirm also that that body was not there when you arrived? This is paragraph 39, letter E, of your witness statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you be more precise as to the where?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: First of all, perhaps you could just help us with this. You were shown a set of photographs by Mr. Kelly, if we look at 39 A of your witness statement, and you referred there to two colour photographs of bodies that you did not recall seeing. One of those you've described as photo 122. Now what I'm showing you here behind tab 4 B is photograph 123, taken in the area towards the foot of the falls. In other words, in the natural section of the canal, beneath the falls. Did you see that body, Witness 64?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can see it, but I have to tell you that I don't recognise those photographs at all. I don't know anything about them. Kelly showed me those photographs and I told him that I had not made those photographs and that I could not recognise the body.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. That's the second half of that answer I just want to tease out. That body wasn't there when you arrived, was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, no. I know nothing about those photographs. I can't recognise the photographs. I can't recognise the bodies. I really don't know what this depicts, what this is in relation to.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And then finally, in relation to those first two bodies that you looked at behind tab 1, at paragraph 112 of your witness statement, you say this: "Photograph number 2 shows two bodies in bright colours and they appear not to be too badly decomposed, but I did not see them during my work at Lake Radonjic, from the 11th of September until the investigation was finished." I simply want to ask you this, Witness 64. Does it follow from that answer that despite videoing each set of remains removed from the canal section, you did not ever see those two bodies removed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct. It is correct that those two bodies that I see now in front of me in the canal, that to the best of my recollection, they had not been pulled out. I'm sure about it. When this photograph was first shown to me, it was dated the 8th of September 1998, and the first time that I got there on the site was the 11th. And from -- just a moment, sir, please allow me to finish. I mentioned the date of the 8th of September, and from the report of the hydrometeorological institute, we know that there was this big thunder-storm and heavy rain on that day that washed away those bodies.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (redacted) Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You did see all of the bodies removed from the canyon --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You did see, Witness 64, all of the bodies removed from the canyon section and videoed them, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With the exception of these two, and what you showed me on the pictures. For all the rest, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just to be absolutely clear, from your recollection, these two bodies weren't removed at any time after you arrived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To the best of my recollection, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. At paragraphs 28 --

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could Mr. Emmerson identify -- say after your arrival, is he referring to the concrete part of the canal or the non-concrete part? The question is very vague actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the witness said he arrived on the 11th of September and that Mr. Emmerson was pointing at the photographs showing the two persons in the concrete part of the canal and then later the photographs he just mentioned, the photographs found behind tab 4 in the blue binder, which I think the witness also said that he did not see these bodies being removed. That comes to a total of four, which he has not seen being removed after he arrived on the 11th of September.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think it's three because tab 4 contains two photographs of the same body. It's two bodies in tab 1 of the file.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I agree with you. That was a mistake on my side. You followed this. This is what you testified, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I wonder if I can just ask on another topic, please, paragraphs 28 and 29 of your 92 ter statement, you say that you saw bullet holes in the concrete canal wall and you say: "There were bullet holes on the outer canal wall where I first saw" -- I'm sorry, "where I saw the first five or six bodies were located." And then at paragraph 29 you say: "There were bullet holes on the inside canal wall at the same place where I saw the two bodies in the photograph dated the 8th of September." Now, just to be clear, so that the Trial Chamber can follow the testimony, if you imagine you're looking towards Lake Radonjic, what you are describing in paragraph 28 is seeing bullet holes on the outside of the right wall as you look towards the lake; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. To the left. Look at me now, please. There is this canal where the river flows in the direction of the Radonjic Lake. There was damage to the internal part of the canal and on this side of the canal. So on both walls. On the sides facing the village of Glodjane. That would be the correct way of putting it. On the sides facing the village of Glodjane.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that there is some confusion because from what I see you doing, of course that's not visible on the video, and from what I hear you saying, I get the impression that you do not disagree at all, especially in view of the last portion of what you said. I understand that if you're looking downstream, the Glodjane side of the canal is to the right. You just told us that bullet holes were seen on the outer and inner wall facing Glodjane, which I understand to be again still looking downstream, on the outer side of the right-hand wall and on the inner side of the left-hand wall, both facing Glodjane. Is that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that there is no disagreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, there is in fact disagreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then please sort that out, but now at least we know --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We know what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- what the witness said, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: At paragraph 29 of your statement, you say: "There were bullet holes on the inside canal wall at the same place where I saw the two bodies in the photograph dated the 8th. Those bodies were not there on the 11th." Now we can see from the photograph that those two bodies are located against the inner side of the right-hand wall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There I want to -- this came into my mind when you first put the question to the witness. Let's try first to clarify what the witness meant because that will show us whether there is any disagreement, yes or no. When you said the place where you saw the bodies that were photographed on the 8th, yes, were you meaning to say at that side of the wall or approximately so much downstream as where these bodies were located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. The bullet holes or impact holes have nothing to do with the -- these two bodies. I'm merely describing the place where I found them. I am describing those places on this concrete wall where I saw those bullet holes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: (redacted), what I want to suggest to you is that there were also bullet holes in the outer aspect of the left-hand wall and on the inner aspect of the right-hand wall firing, therefore, in the opposite direction. Do you agree with that or not? If not, we can play you a portion of the video you took.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir, please listen to me. Let me explain this for you once and for all. If you look towards Radonjic Lake, the bullet holes were found on the left-hand side wall, on the inner aspect, facing the village of Glodjane, and on the right-hand side wall, on the outer aspect, again facing the village of Glodjane.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I understand that that's your testimony --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Witness 64. I'm putting a specific suggestion to you. You're suggesting to the Trial Chamber that the bullet holes that were seen were all fired from the Glodjane side of the canal. And I'm suggesting to you that, on the contrary, there were bullet marks on the outer aspect of the left-hand wall having been fired in the opposite direction as well. Now, can you help us with that? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct. Yes, it is recorded on the footage at one point, where, from the other -- the outer side of the left-hand side wall facing Radonjic Lake, or if you look in the direction of Radonjic Lake, there are some bullet holes, and then you can see a dead dog, I think, a white dog. It's dead. But we didn't find any bodies there in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I understand that but just so that we have it absolutely clear for the record, there was evidence of shots being fired in the opposite direction, towards the Gllogjan side. That's correct, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There are a few bullet holes, yes. That can be seen on the footage, on the video recording. That's for sure, yes. But the majority is on the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. I have just one or two very short questions, if I may. Paragraph 39 E of your witness statement, you refer to some photographs of a body in a field which you say were an entirely different scene and nothing to do with Lake Radonjic. I think it's right to say you videoed that body in the field, did you not, as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is not completely clear to me. First you talk about the photograph, and then you say that I took it. So I don't know -- I don't understand the way you phrase your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We've all had an opportunity to look at the footage that you produced, Witness 64, and included in it is some footage of a body seen in a field which appears to be very similar to the photograph that you're referring to in your witness statement. Do you remember, whilst you were involved in this process, videoing a body in a field some considerable distance away?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Yes, I'm sure two or three bodies. I recorded two or three bodies in the nearby villages. Because at that time, you have to know that Judge Gojkovic was there in -- on the site that we are talking about, and as soon as a body would be found, I would accompany him there to those estates where those bodies were found. So I'm absolutely sure, I remember that we were there, yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We have no interpretation. As a matter of fact, I was -- could you please repeat? I was following your French, Mr. Dutertre, so I didn't look at my screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Might be a bit late but I would love Mr. Emmerson to show us the photos he's talking about which nobody can see on the screen so we don't really see what we are referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I can certainly produce them to Mr. Dutertre, they are his own exhibit but I'm sure we can assist him to find them. But may I pursue the matter in a slightly different way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see there seems to be some --

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know where they are but maybe the Court --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, there seems to be some confusion about photographs and having videoed because the witness in response to your question about photographs said that he was sent to other places where he videoed the matter, so that confuses me a bit. So before we look at photographs or videos in detail, could we please first clarify this?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Witness 64, if you could just answer my next question yes or no, was there an occasion after you arrived on the 11th, when you took video footage of at least one body in an entirely separate location?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: How many occasions did that occur between the 11th, when you arrived, and the time when you left? In other words, how many bodies in unrelated locations did you video?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For the 11th, the first day, we had a body found there at the farm, between the barns. That's the body marked with number 1. I'm sure about that. And later on, I think there were maybe two other bodies that were found on some other unrelated locations. Everything else comes from the canal, from the village of Glodjane.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I just want to be absolutely clear so that we avoid any possible confusion. You never went to the village of Dasinoc where some remains were recovered, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, never, never. I never went to Dasinovac. I know who was found there, I'm perfectly clear but I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You never went to Dasinoc if you leave aside the body that was found at the economic farm, how many other bodies in unrelated locations did you see and video between the time of your arrival, on the 11th, and the time you left the area some days later?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, two or three bodies, not more than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, I'm looking at the clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm pretty much finished. I just wanted to ask the witness this.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: What happened if you know to those bodies, in other words, where were they taken for forensic examination if they were?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think they are being a bit confused now but maybe Mr. Emmerson could clarify this point and I'm sure he will do so. Could he ask the witness where the witness has recorded, in what area has he recorded the other two cases he referred to. The other two bodies he referred to. Because we don't know what happened to these bodies but I believe that we should do things in the right order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it wouldn't be a bad idea to know where it was but first, perhaps, the witness answers the question, short, clear question. These two or not more than three bodies, do you recall where they were taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't now say with absolute certainty but they should be at -- should have been at the Pastrik Hotel in this make-shift morgue there at Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Another question: This unrelated location, could you tell us where that approximately was? So where the two or three bodies were found, which you said were taken probably to Hotel Pastrik.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was in the Decani municipality, but I can't give you the exact location. I can't remember that. But I know that it was close to Decani, villages around Decani. But now, as for the exact location, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Those are my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: These are your questions. Then we'll have a break and after the break, Mr. Guy-Smith and Mr. Harvey will have an opportunity to further question you. We have a break until 25 minutes to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith. Witness 64, Mr. Guy-Smith is counsel for Mr. Balaj. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Witness 64, at paragraph 47 of your 92 ter statement, you state that you turned your video camera off because you had to get from one place to the other by car. In the statement that you made on the 23rd of 2007, in the same paragraph, paragraph 47, you indicated that you turned your video recorder off because you had to walk from one place to the other. That's of less consequence than the following question that I have to you, which is during the time that you were videoing the scenes, how many times did you turn your video recorder off?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Several times. Several times. Whenever I had to change the position from which I was filming, I had to switch the video camera off so that there wouldn't be any changes or inconsistencies in the footage due to these breaks. That's why I had to switch it off so that we wouldn't have these -- that panning left and right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, apart from switching it off, as you just indicated, so there wouldn't be any breaks when you were changing from one position to another, did you turn your video camera off at any other time, at the direction of any of the individuals who were leading the investigation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I never received such orders, nor would I expect any such orders, because the assignment was to film as much as possible. There wasn't anyone in situ who would have been able to order something like that to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you say that you were given the direction or the assignment to film as much as possible, who was that direction given to you by?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You misunderstood me. It's not that I'm receiving an order or an assignment from anyone. That's my opinion. And as a crime-scene technician, out in the field, I have the intention to film as much as possible in order to allow the investigation to take the right course.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: During the time that you were video recording, were various people who were involved in the investigation pointing things out to you to have filmed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They probably were. Members of the forensic team. Because as professionals in their own field, they were able to see some things more clearly than I was, and it is quite possible that they insisted that I film something that they thought was quite important. Otherwise, any other person wouldn't figure as importantly or be as relevant as they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: During the time that you were video recording the various scenes, were you ever directed not to film any scenes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, certainly not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you gave your what I'll call your 92 bis statement, which is a statement that you made on June 23rd of this year, the statement you made in Belgrade, that you spoke with Mr. Emmerson about, the statement that you attested to and said it was true, I'd like to refer to you paragraph 11 and the best way for you to probably do that is to look at what is called tab 9 in the green binder. I think that you also may have a copy of it in B/C/S because there may have been a problem before we made a copy available in B/C/S. Let me correct that. Let me get you this copy. If you could -- if you could give him the copy in B/C/S, paragraph 11.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I found it.
