utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And my question to you, sir, is with regard to the very last sentence in paragraph 11. You stated, "The only time the police would not record a scene being pointed out by a witness would be when it would not be in the best interests of the investigation." Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, this does not relate to me at all. This is just an off-hand remark that I made, and in my opinion, it has been badly mistranslated because I was not at the scene first, and I was not the first person to see the scene.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you say this was an off-hand remark that you made, I'd like to ask you, is it not accurate that on the 23rd of June, you had an opportunity to review your entire statement including this paragraph with this specific language before you attested to it, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I read it most likely, but in that context, in a broader context, it didn't mean anything. This was just an arbitrary comment. It had nothing to do with me. It didn't refer to me. So I didn't insist on it being changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, as a matter of fact, in the same statement, at paragraph 120, you stated, "This statement was provided for me on the 23rd June 2007, translated into Serbian, and as such, I acknowledge it as my own." That was true when you said it then, and that's true now, correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I agree with you, yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You continue by saying on 23rd June 2007, "I was invited to add things which I deemed necessary and make changes where I deemed necessary. I have added these things and made corrections because I had mentioned them while I was giving my statement but they were not included in my statement. This statement is true." That's what you said at the time that you attested to the statement on the 23rd of June, and that is correct as you sit here today, is it not, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, the attestation of the 23rd of June has been covered. Let's go to the substance. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: In paragraph 11 of your 92 ter statement, the statement that you have submitted and the statement that was made on the 23rd, 24th and 27th of August, that particular sentence has been deleted, has it not, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: My question is this: When you met with the Prosecution on the 23rd, the 24th and the 27th of August, did you have discussions with them about your 92 bis statement and by that I mean the statement that you made on 23rd of June 2007, paragraph by paragraph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, definitely.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: To your knowledge, were those discussions recorded?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean discussions between me and the investigator?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Discussions that you had between yourself and the individuals who you met with on the 23rd, 4th and 7th of August.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, to be quite honest, I don't know whether it was recorded anywhere. At least I was not told that what we were talking about was recorded on any kind of media.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: During that time, on the 23rd, 24th and 27th of August, to your knowledge were notes being taken of the conversation that you were having with investigators and members of the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to know how relevant these questions are regarding the matter we are dealing with today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, of course you may respond but it's rather obvious, Mr. Guy-Smith, but please correct me if I'm wrong, is testing the accuracy, completeness of the statements given by the witness, whether there is any other information given to the OTP which is not reflected. I take it that that's your purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That is indeed one of my purposes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then that makes it sufficiently relevant. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: During the time that you were having the conversations on the three dates that have been mentioned, did you discuss with members of the OTP the prior testimony of other people who had appeared before this Chamber?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I understood your question correctly, you're asking me if we discussed prior witnesses that appeared.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. We never discussed any witnesses. I don't know who testified before my evidence and we never, ever talked about that at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And did you discuss what evidence had been placed before the Chamber prior to your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no. Absolutely. No, no, I don't -- no, I'm sure we didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the statement that you made at paragraph 77 of your 92 ter statement, sir, you stated, "The Trial Chamber also has access to the forensic experts' reports so they can check the allegations contained in my statement." Is that a matter that you discussed with the OTP during the time that you were preparing your 92 ter statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, most probably we did, regarding R-19, that body, and when I said that I thought it was Tush Frrokaj, expressing my own opinion, I said that if the Trial Chamber deems it necessary, they can compare my statement with other evidence or other reports provided by the experts. We never discussed this in any greater detail than that. That was the extent of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Were you aware of the exhibits that had been introduced with regard to R-19? And by that, I mean was this a matter of discussion that you had with the OTP since you used the word "most probably," used the phrase, "Most probably we did."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. What I'm telling you is that I was the one who brought up the possibility that the Trial Chamber could compare my testimony, my statement, with the evidence or reports provided by forensic medicine specialists because I claim that the body -- because it's just this fact that needed to be corroborated by other evidence, to check whether this is recorded as a body. This is the first time that I hear from you that you have some evidence related to R-19. I have absolutely no knowledge of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: After you made the statement on June 23rd, and before you met with the OTP in August, were you supplied material from the MUP, which you sat down and reviewed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, certainly, yes, of course. I officially requested from the war crimes department, where all this has been filed, all this material, to be allowed to inspect my video recordings that I had made in 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And did you inform the Office of the Prosecutor that you had done that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, to tell you the truth, I can't remember. I don't remember, really.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: During the conversation you had with the Prosecution for three days in preparation of your 92 ter statement, did you discuss with them that you had reviewed information outside of their presence after you had made the statement on June 23rd?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, probably I did. I may have said that I disagreed with some parts of my statement, either because it had been mistranslated or because I had said something that was not correct, now that I've gone through my materials and verified what the actual situation was, I said that I would make some corrections to my statement. So I may have said something like that. But I don't think that it is of any major importance. That's not something that I gave a lot of thought to.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, I appreciate that. With regard to the concerns you had about your statement of June 23rd being either mistranslated or because something you had said was not correct, did you tell the Office of the Prosecutor on those three days specifically what you thought was mistranslated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I probably did, and given time, I would be able to identify those parts in my statement. I'm sure that I indicated that it was mistranslated -- that it was a mistranslation in my first statement where I said that fire brigade ladder was used to pull out bodies of the Frrokaj couple. I'm sure that it was a mistranslation. That's not what I said. And there are numerous instances of this sort. It's enough for just one word to be wrong for the whole thing to come out in a completely wrong way.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, the matter that you've just discussed, which is paragraph 32 of your 92 bis statement that you gave on June 23rd that you are indicating was mistranslated, that was something that you had an opportunity to review on the 23rd. At that time you found no fault with your statement, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I read the statement several times, and whenever I went through it again, I would find something that was either a mistranslation or a mistake or something of that sort. I'm sure that if I were to read it again, I would probably find some typos or some things that would catch my eye.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Just so we are clear and there is no confusion, it is your position that with regard to the following words being spoken, which is, "The two bodies in the canyon where the red Opel Kadett was located were recovered with the assistance of the fire brigade who gave us a ladder to get down to the canyon and a rope to haul the body bags with the body inside up to ground level," was mistranslated?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This question has already been put to the witness, who has already answered the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Nevertheless, the witness is -- the question is put to the witness in a bit of a different way, and, therefore, the witness should answer that question. You remember the question, Mr. Guy-Smith just read a portion of your statement that: "The two bodies in the canyon where the red Opel Kadett was located were recovered with the assistance of the fire brigade who gave us a ladder to get down to the canyon and a rope to haul the body bags with the body inside up to ground level." The question was whether this was mistranslated or --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know what it was, whether it was a mistranslation or an addition. I know, because I was there on the scene, that there, where the female body was found next to this Opel Kadett car, the fire brigade ladder was not put in. It was used downstream, maybe 300 to 400 metres away but not there at that site.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes. When you were in Belgrade on the 23rd of June and you were making this statement, you were read rules concerning what could potentially occur if you made a false statement, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Am I supposed to answer? I didn't understand this to be a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Let me rephrase?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question was whether such a rule was read to you because at that time it was still considered just to introduce your statement without your presence, and then the rules require to inform the witness that if his statement is not in accordance with the truth, that he might get punished for that. Was that read to you? That's the simple question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I only speak the truth, ever, so there was no need for that to be read to me. I was fully, and I am fully, aware of that. I'm aware of what I have to do while I'm here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question simply was whether it was read to you. Whether there was any need or not is a different question, but Mr. Guy-Smith just asked you whether this was read because the rules require for such a statement that this is read to the witness. Not because of you but because of the rules primarily.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember that being read to me. I got the rules. I was handed the rules. And I am fully familiar with the contents of the rules.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You understood at the time you made this statement on 23rd of June the importance of what you were saying --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, I earlier said that the attestation of the 23rd of June had been -- I mean, it's perfectly clear that you consider this to be an important matter and you'd like to perhaps ask the witness five, six or seven times whether he thought it important.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The point is clear. Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you met with the Prosecution in August, did you bring notes with you concerning those errors that you believed existed in the statement that you had made on June 23rd, 2007?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, definitely, I brought my notes with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And the notes that you brought with you are notes that you, obviously, shared with the Prosecution in making the 92 ter statement, the statement that you have sworn to here today, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't show my notes to anyone. I use my notes as some kind of an aide-memoire. I consider this statement to be my statement, and I represent to you now that it is the truth, my 92 ter statement. That's what it is. I would like you to point me to something that is not correct in it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's not enter into any debate. First of all, Mr. Guy-Smith, page 65, line 10 --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- may I take it that it is 2006?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No, 2007 because that was the date he attested to it. The statement was initially made in 2006. He read it and attested to it on 23rd of June 2007. That's why I'm using that day because it's between the 23rd of June 2007 and the August date that that's the time that there have been any shifts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm afraid that we do not have the attestation at this moment here in front of us so that has been clarified and now --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That was a subject matter of a 92 bis application, motion by the Prosecution sometime ago. I don't know whether we need to put that in evidence with regard to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that it's part, annexed to one of the submissions although, of course, the Chamber at this moment knowing that the witness would appear that we would operate under Rule 92 ter rather than 92 bis has not paid any further attention to it at this very moment. So therefore, that was correct, 2007. Could there be any confusion as to the notes? Because that's what came into my mind. When you said you brought your notes with you, were these the notes you originally had made or did you make specific notes on any mistakes or matters that needed correction in your 2006 statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I prepared the notes the moment when the statement was made available to me in Serbian, and then I was able to ascertain where the mistakes are and later on, of course, once I was allowed to review my video recordings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: So we are perfectly clear, when you made notes in June of 2007, was it at that point in time, before you signed the statement, that you recognised that there were mistakes?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Chairman, Your Honour, this question was put on several occasions. It has been repeated on several times and I was wondering whether it is useful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do agree with you, Mr. Dutertre, that similar questions, although always in a tiny different shape, are put to the witness. Therefore, Mr. Guy-Smith is encouraged not to.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Slightly deviate in a little bit of a different way? I understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Finally, with regard to the time that you made the statement on the 23rd through the 27th of August, those three days, 23rd, 24th and 27th, at that point in time, when you were making what you call your corrections to your previous statement, did you have a discussion with the Prosecution about those corrections?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, naturally, I did discuss it, but not in the sense of whether I should enter my corrections or not. The only thing I discussed with the Prosecution is that I found those mistakes, inaccuracies, and that I insisted that they be corrected in the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions. But I do once again ask for that which I asked prior to this witness's testimony, which I am told does not exist, which are any proofing notes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Whether there are any proofing notes. Of course, in comparing these statements, we have seen that there are some differences but major parts are literally the same. Mr. Dutertre, are there any proofing notes you made? Or any of your team members?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is no proofing note made for the 23rd, 4th and 27th of August. The position has always been clear. Either we had signed proofing notes or 92 ter signed. So things are very clear. And they are so clear that we have many various interpretations of the witness concerning the previous and the present version. He has signed one version on the 27th, which corresponds to the testimony made with the modifications and the corrections he decided to introduce.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I don't think this is the appropriate time to go back and revisit the issue of proofing notes but, obviously, you see the dilemma we find ourselves in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Harvey, any questions for Witness 64?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: No, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre -- let me first --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre, is there any need to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I try to be rather brief. Re-examination by Mr. Dutertre

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: First question to Witness 64. We have what you discussed now where you have signed 92 bis statement on June the 24th and then you signed a 92 ter on August the 27th, recently, and you have indicated, and it's on page 61 of today's transcript, that on -- between June and August, you had access to your footage. My question is the following: On 23rd of June, when Mr. Versonnen asked to you sign a 92 bis, did he show you your videos, your footage, which are the subject of this hearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Do you mean Mr. Barney Kelly?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No, Mr. Versonnen on June the 23rd, last when you signed your 92 bis statement.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know the gentleman. I don't know him. I know that he was mentioned as the person who sought the material from the MUP, and that the MUP staff provided him with the material sought, which he in turn handed to Mr. Barney Kelly, but I don't think I ever met the gentleman.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Understood. Name of the people doesn't really matter. On June 2007, have you seen the videos which are the subject of this -- of your statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If you mean to say or ask whether I personally saw the video, yes, but when I was talking to investigators, I saw some clips of these recordings.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: On June the 23rd, when you signed this 92 bis statement in the field office in Belgrade, were you able to see this video?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like us to see video P452, with the number ERN 0006-6012, from 14 -- second 14 to minute 1, 15, 37 seconds. And he refers to the starting point of 16 hours and 36 on September the 16th. Can we see this video?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can stop now, and it will be a minute 15.05.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Witness 64, in your 92 ter statement you said, and I quote, [In English] "At 16.36 on 12 September 1998 -- 1998, I video recorded downstream of the canyon where I focused on a body from approximately 100 to 150 metres which could have been dressed in red-pink clothing or maybe the skin was that colour at the moment due to the decomposition of the body and weather conditions. The divers told us about this body as they passed on their way back up the canyon from the lake. Seeing this body now, it could be the body that I saw with bright clothing in the photograph dated 8 September 1998." [Interpretation] My question is the following for Witness 64: Has this body been collected later?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. This body was never recovered, was never pulled out.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: What are the reasons why it was not recovered later, Witness 64?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because on that day, we had a terrorist attack already at the time when we were in the canal doing our work. We were just about to recover this body when the investigating judge ordered that we stop working. In the coming days, the weather worsened and I believe that the water flow washed the body away in the direction of Lake Radonjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have no more questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Dutertre. Have the questions in re-examination triggered any need to further examine the witness? Witness 64, this then concludes your testimony before this Trial Chamber. We would like to thank you very much. Unfortunately, you had to wait for a while before you could give your testimony, but finally, you have now given it, you've answered the questions put to you by the parties and by the Bench and I'd like to thank you for coming and I wish you a safe trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before I ask Madam Usher to escort you out of the courtroom, are there any attachments or any exhibits we have not dealt with at this very moment, attachments to the 92 ter statement it's a bit difficult for us to because we received only today the final version. Were there any attachments to it?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. There were four annexes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are these the photographs shown to the witness which were given the numbers PBK or something like that? Is that -- are these the annexes?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the Defence team, I don't know, but regarding annex 1 and annex 4, they certainly include these photos. And as to annex 3 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have the 92 ter statement on my screen, and that is 20 pages. I see no annexes. Have they been separately tendered? Do they need separate numbers?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Actually, for the statement, just to avoid repeating ERNs for documents already having an ERN number, based on your suggestion, we have avoided annexing them in 92 ter. Therefore, they should be given a separate number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we should ask for a separate number. Are these photographs shown to the witness, are they not yet exhibits? I mean, I can imagine that some of the photographs, I don't see them for the first time today, so therefore, I wonder whether they have already exhibit numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Some of them do but they are shown in a format which is not the one we used previously. We had the photo albums, we also had photos of four pages so therefore, the photo we are interested in is tendered but what the witness had been shown at that time does not exactly correspond to the photos we have here. For instance, just to be clear, annex 1 has four photos.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have again -- I have in front of me a 92 ter statement, a redacted version, that's the one that's tendered today, that's 20 pages, and I -- where do I find at this moment the annexes, Mr. Dutertre? Because --

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, on August the 28th, 2007, we sent the Chamber an e-mail with all the documents including the annexes, and there was an Excel table where you have the reference of all these annexes. It's an e-mail which was sent at 6.24 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You can give me the date?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was on August 28th, 2007, at 6.24. It was sent to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 6.24 p.m., I take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It was not sent precisely to you, but Mr. Zahar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Usually, if there is anything which needs our direct attention, Mr. Zahar would then pass that on to us. But apart from that, even if you sent -- even if you sent --

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there is something new in it, it should be properly introduced in evidence in this courtroom. Is the -- are the Defence teams aware of the exact data given by Mr. Dutertre?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before that he had this document before him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There seems to be kind of a table which -- annexes to the 92 ter statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I can see the table. We have the table.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. On the basis of that, could I ask the Defence whether there is any objection against admission of these annexes apart from the 92 ter statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The short answer to that question is yes, there is an objection, as matters currently stand. I'm sorry it's slightly obscure at the moment on my screen. I do apologise. Annex 2 is the meteorological data which in our submission is not properly produced by this witness and the photographs that cross-refer to paragraph 15, which were dealt with in chief, again we object to the admission of those.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And these were the photographs of one with the wrong -- two photographs, the top one being identified not as the person who appears in that photograph, and the -- yes. That's -- I take it, then, relevance objection. Any other objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In fact, the next three comprises a multitude of photographs, a series of photographs, which are both post mortem of the body of Captain Perovic. The weapons which had been photographed in the village where his body was recovered, as well as damages -- damage to a house. Those are elements which have -- would evidence the attacks against civilians, and that's why there is a reference at the end of the paragraph 15 and 112 to 115.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any other objections against that?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No, but that's a specific objection that has been specifically made to paragraphs, the annexes which are annex 3 and the information contained in paragraphs 113, 14 and 15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, if I would have a complete overview here, we could immediately deal with it, but I do not feel at this moment in a position to finally deal with the matter. Mr. Dutertre, you are invited to provide the list of annexes to the extent that these annexes are already in evidence, to point at that, and then we can decide on the matter as soon as possible, and we have already on the record objections against the meteorological data and some photographs, especially annex 3 but also the two pictures of another victim unrelated to the Lake Radonjic canal. When I say victim, I say this in the general term that the two persons shown there died, nothing more, nothing less.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I don't pursue further submissions in relation to, although Your Honours will recall the testimony of the last witness in connection with that sequence of events. I wonder if I could just, just before the witness departs, invite him to remove his ear phones just for one moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Witness 64, first of all, do you understand English? You do understand some English, isn't it? Do you understand --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, I don't understand it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then would you please take off your ear phones for a second? Mr. Emmerson?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the penultimate sentence in paragraph 112 of the 92 ter statement, that is the last unredacted sentence, which is a matter which I took the witness to and he confirmed on oath --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just -- you said paragraph?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Where the witness confirms not only that the two bodies floating in the concrete section of the canal were not recovered, but that he did not see them again at any time between his arrival and his departure. Now, I'm not asking anybody to pursue the matter further, but it is plain that that answer cannot be reconciled with the answer elicited by Mr. Dutertre in re-examination, in our submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but it is for the Chamber to appraise the answer to the questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm content to leave the matter that way but lest there should be no misunderstanding that there is a categorical statement to that effect in the 92 ter statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's clear. We'll not restart any examination of the witness on the matter. Witness 64, you had to wait a while. We just -- yes, could you please put your ear phones again? We asked to you wait for a second to see whether we would still need you for the admission of the evidence. It turns out that we can deal with the matter in your absence. Therefore, you are excused. Madam Usher, could you escort the witness out of the courtroom after you've pulled down the curtains?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I was just provided by the Chamber's staff with a copy of the table. We'll deal with the matter once we have given it a more thorough look. Yes. Do I understand that the booth have received copies of a decision on protective measures for Witness 3? That is the witness to follow. I'm listening to the English channel at this moment. We usually provide the booth copies of decisions given orally which, however, we write down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The logistics in the Chamber have not functioned properly at this moment. I therefore, although we try to avoid to do that, but perhaps we will first -- no, we keep the curtains down for a moment. We are not in private session, although with the curtains down we are in open session. The Chamber grants the protective measures requested for Witness 3. That is face distortion, voice distortion, and pseudonym. Now, the question is, Mr. Registrar, do we have to adapt the voice distortion for the next witness before we can start?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that that has been taken care of. That means, Mr. Di Fazio, are you calling your next witness, Witness 3? MR. DI FAZIO: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, the curtains are down at this moment in view of the protective measures granted. The witness first will have to enter the courtroom and we'll then pull the curtains up. Madam Usher left the courtroom I hope also to escort Witness 3 into the courtroom. Mr. Di Fazio, may I expect that you'll use the August 2007 statement as 92 ter statements or --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I don't believe -- MR. DI FAZIO: No, I intend to lead his evidence orally. There is no question about that. Defence counsel jumping to their feet there, they don't need to worry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness 3, because that's how we will call you, first of all, can you hear me in a language you understand? Can you hear me in a language you understand, Witness? Could you please speak more loudly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness 3, before you give evidence in this Court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require to you make a solemn declaration that you will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration, of which the text is now handed out to you by Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness 3, please be seated. Madam Usher, the curtains can be drawn up. Witness 3, the Chamber has decided that the request for protective measures are granted. That means that we will call you not by your own name but we'll call you Witness 3, and your voice and your face will not be recognisable outside this courtroom. However, the content of your testimony is public. Mr. Di Fazio -- oh, yes, I would like to add to that, if there ever is a question where you would fear that answering that question in public might expose other persons to any risk, as far as security is concerned, please let me know. We will then consider whether or not to go into private session. Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. And I might add that if I have any questions that might tend to elicit evidence that will identify this witness, I'll also seek the Court's permission to go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please does so. Examination by Mr. Di Fazio

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. Can the witness be shown 65 ter 1965. Witness, have a look at the document that you're going to see on your screen and look an and read it, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The document we admitted under seal should not be shown to the public. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, in that case, that should not occur and I have a hard copy which I can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the technicians can perfectly show it to the witness and not to the outside world. MR. DI FAZIO: I'm grateful for that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. Just look at that and tell us if the personal details that you see written there are correct.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/3
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please come a bit closer to the microphone which makes it easier for the interpreters to hear you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Everything is correct. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, and if Your Honours please I seek to tender that pseudonym sheet into evidence and ask that it be placed under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, that would be number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P913, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that there is no objection against it being admitted. Therefore, it's admitted into evidence. Please proceed. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I have some further personal particulars that I need to elicit from this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll turn into private session, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Please proceed, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, there is no need to refer to the name of your village. I want to ask you, in your village, was the LDK a popular party?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/3
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Can you give the Trial Chamber some idea of the extent of popularity enjoyed by the LDK in your village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/3
utterances.text: At that time, before the war, the LDK was a very popular party in the whole of the territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And that might be so, but listen to the question. I'm asking about your particular village, in particular. No need to mention the name of it, but in your village, was it a -- what was the extent of its popularity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/3
utterances.text: Everybody in my village was an LDK member before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Was that fact, the fact of the extent of popularity in your village of the LDK, was that known in the wider area, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is both leading and calls for speculation on behalf of the witness. I would ask Mr. Di Fazio to be very careful about leading throughout this testimony, and I think he knows exactly what the issues are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, you're invited to reformulate the question, not to deal with the matter but in a different way. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you ever have an opportunity to assess what other people in your area knew about the political persuasion of your village? Did you ever have a chance to do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/3
utterances.text: I'm referring to the period before the war, and before the war there was no other party but the LDK, and so the majority of the population supported it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: All right. Well, I'll move on. In your village, your particular village, was there a village guard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/3
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Who organised that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/3
utterances.text: The villagers.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Was there any participation of the LDK political party in its organisation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/3
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And from when was that village guard organised? When did it first commence, so to speak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/3
utterances.text: I can't be very precise, but I think it began sometime in 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Were you a member of that village guard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/3
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And did that village guard exist in your village in the months leading up to May of 1998?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/3
utterances.text: Not after May 1998, no, not in the same way it did before.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, we'll get to that, but up until about at least mid -- up until the 19th of May 1998, did it exist?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/3
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. I want you to turn your mind to events in May of 1998, and I'm talking about the period of time now prior to the 19th of May. At that time, or during that time, did your village receive any visits by any KLA officers or members?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/3
utterances.text: Do you mean May?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes. I mean the period of time prior to May of -- prior to May 19th, 1998. Did your village receive, as far as you're aware, any visits by KLA men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/3
utterances.text: Yes. That's what they say but I was not present myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, I don't want you to mention any names but what are you referring to when you say you were not present yourself? What weren't you present at, first of all, and then tell us what you know about whatever you were not present at.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/3
utterances.text: When they entered the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Can you tell us who you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/3
utterances.text: I'm referring to the KLA at the point of entry into the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Using the 19th of May 1998 as a reference point, can you say when the KLA appeared at your village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/3
utterances.text: I first saw KLA men in uniforms in my village for the first time on the 19th of May, but they say it was present before but I hadn't been there. However, on the 19th I was there to see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Did you have any idea of a KLA presence prior to the 19th of May, even if you did not see them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/3
utterances.text: I certainly wished they existed but some people, but people disagreed. Some people said the KLA exists, some others said it doesn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you know Lahi Brahimaj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/3
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Prior to the 19th of May 1998, did he go to your village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/3
utterances.text: That's what people say but I was never present.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey? I apologise for not having --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Not at all, Your Honour. I was up and I was down again but this is all rather speculative and at least the witness is being clear but I think the questions -- a question such as did Mr. Brahimaj ever go to his village is vague and not particularly helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is soliciting an answer to whether the witness has any recollection of Lahi Brahimaj going to his village.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: We have that answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Prior to the 19th of May 1998, in your village, were there any meetings that -- attended by the KLA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/3
utterances.text: Again, that's what people say but I was never present.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Fine. We've heard you and we now understand very, very clearly that you weren't present. But you have said that's what people say. Now, I want to know exactly and precisely what you heard from people, who you heard things from, and what you heard about this. And remember, don't mention names of villagers unless -- yes, don't mention names of villagers.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, with respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's an invitation. If you would mention any name of villagers where you are not confident that it would be without risk, then you should ask to go into private session before giving any such names. Is that clear to you? So if you want to say I heard this from X, Y or Z, and if you're not confident that -- or if you fear that this might have negative consequences for X, Y or Z, then you should ask me to go into private session because then you give the names without the whole of the world hearing them. Is that clear, Witness 3?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it's very clear. And even if I were to give the name, there wouldn't be any risk because he no longer lives. He was a former commander in my village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course, if there are no risks, then there is no need but please keep this in mind. Would you please then answer the question put to you by Mr. Di Fazio saying that from whom you heard, and exactly what about, from these people, even though you were not present.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I spoke to Sadri Berisha, who used to be the commander of our village. He had just been nominated a commander in charge of the youth of our village. And he requested of me to join the KLA, which at that stage complied with my wishes as well. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. Earlier you said that people had said that there was a meeting involving the KLA. That's what I'm interested in, a meeting in your village concerning -- involving the KLA. What did you hear about that and from whom did you hear about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/3
utterances.text: I heard from the villagers themselves that they had been there, and in time, the youth of the village started joining the KLA ranks.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Now, what did you hear precisely that they -- stating that they had been there? What sort of details did you get from your fellow villagers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/3
utterances.text: At the time there were various rumours on the existence of the KLA. The people were not certain of it, and so it was a pleasure to know it, that there was a KLA when they appeared in the village and from that moment onwards the youth of the village began joining them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. You've told us that you found out about this KLA appearing in the village from your fellow villagers. Do you know which KLA representatives attended? Did you have any information about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/3
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Who attended?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/3
utterances.text: I have no idea on who it was. Rumours have it that it was Lahi but having not been present myself, I cannot say it. I mean some people might say he had been there but even that person might not have been there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. Did your village have a mill?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/3
utterances.text: Yes, it did. And it was a necessary thing to have.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Can you tell the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, perhaps one question to clarify matters. You said rumours have it that it was Lahi but having not been present myself, you can't say that. Now, did you hear from other villagers that Lahi had been present?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I did hear from the villagers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, did these villagers also tell you that they themselves had been present?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I never asked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. But did they even sometimes without being asked, people, did they say something about the meeting or --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. They did not say that they had attended or whether they dined with Lahi or anything of the matter, no. They simply said a group had shown themselves and that the KLA really existed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You just told His Honour that they, I assume you mean the villagers, said that a group had shown themselves and that the KLA really existed. Did you understand from what the villagers said to you that when this group showed itself and showed that the KLA really existed, that that was the same occasion in which Lahi Brahimaj came to your village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/3
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, this is as logical a time for the break as any.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Witness 3, it's 7.00. We adjourn for the day. I'd like to instruct you that you should not speak with anyone about the testimony, neither about the testimony you have already given or testimony still to be given. We adjourn until tomorrow, quarter past 2.00, Courtroom III.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
